NexGen Research Showcase

Good research should have somewhere to be shared.

The NexGen Research Showcase is open to anyone with research to share, across all disciplines and career stages. Students, graduates, academics, professionals and independent researchers are equally welcome. University affiliation is not required.

Researchers can submit completed work, ongoing studies or research-based projects for consideration. Selected work can progress to presentation through the NexGen Open Research Symposium, creating a space for different disciplines to meet, exchange ideas and see how other people approach problems.

The purpose is simple: give people a place to share serious work, hear perspectives beyond their own field and learn from one another.

Start a research submission →
Open across disciplines Everyone has a chance to share and learn.

Anyone with research to share can submit, regardless of affiliation or career stage. Interdisciplinary and non-technical research are welcome too.

01

Submit an initial abstract

Share the title, field, research stage and a concise abstract. An initial submission does not require a full paper.

02

Scientific screening

Submissions are screened for relevance, research quality, ethical considerations and suitability for public presentation.

03

Present

Accepted researchers may be invited to prepare and present an A1 research poster at the NexGen Open Research Symposium.

04

Learn from each other

The showcase brings different fields into the same room so researchers can discuss their work, hear other perspectives and take new ideas back into their own research.

NexGen Open Research Symposium

Everyone has something to learn. Everyone has something to teach.

The NexGen Open Research Symposium is the presentation event connected to the Research Showcase. It brings researchers from different fields together to share their work and learn from the way other people think.

A medical researcher may hear something useful from an engineer. Someone in AI may see a question differently after speaking with a designer, educator or biologist. That exchange is part of research too.

What matters: Research does not stop at presentation. It continues through the questions, perspectives and connections that follow.

Open to curiosity

A place to learn with other people.

Different starting points are welcome. NexGen welcomes people at different ages, backgrounds and levels of experience. Some programs are introductory, while others are more technical and have their own age or experience requirements.

Questions are part of learning. NexGen is meant to be a safe, welcoming place to ask questions, try something unfamiliar and exchange ideas without feeling that you are expected to know everything already.

Everyone has something to learn. Everyone has something to teach.

Research, technology and practical development, connected.

NexGen AI Hub Research & Development is a Qatar-based independent research and development initiative that brings together research, emerging technology and practical learning.

We develop projects and programs across artificial intelligence, robotics, biomedical research, quantum technology and other emerging fields, while creating opportunities for people to explore ideas, build skills and share research across disciplines.

At its core, NexGen is about connection. Learners, researchers and different fields can meet in the same space because knowledge grows when it is exchanged.

Accreditation and program status

NexGen is not a university or degree-granting institution. Our workshops, R&D programs and Research Showcase are non-degree, non-credit activities and are not presented as Ministry of Education and Higher Education-accredited academic programs.

Where NexGen issues a certificate, it is a certificate of participation or completion unless explicitly stated otherwise.

NexGen's commercial activity has been applied for under Qatar Business Activity 721007, Artificial Intelligence research and development. Programs are structured as R&D, innovation and exploratory activities connected to that development focus. Any activity requiring separate regulatory approval will only be offered subject to the applicable requirements.

About the Founder

Malak Annan is the founder of NexGen AI Hub Research & Development. She is a Khaleeji woman working across STEM, artificial intelligence and research, with a Master’s in Artificial Intelligence from Ulster University in Qatar and a bachelor’s degree from Carnegie Mellon University in Qatar.

Her work and interests span AI, medical research, robotics, emerging technologies and science education.

Butterflies have always held a special significance for me. Their metamorphosis reflects something I value deeply: growth is not one moment, but a process of becoming. Learning is part of that process, and every new idea can change what comes next.

NexGen is a nexus of everything I am curious about.

It brings together different fields, questions and people in one place, because curiosity rarely stays inside a single subject.

Program status

What participation means

Unless expressly stated otherwise, NexGen programs do not constitute accredited academic qualifications, university credit or professional certification. Certificates, where offered, confirm participation, completion or presentation only.

Research Showcase and Symposium acceptance means acceptance for presentation. It does not by itself constitute peer-reviewed journal publication, academic accreditation, indexing or institutional endorsement of the findings.

Authors retain ownership of their research. Event-specific submission, privacy, photography, publication and intellectual-property terms will be provided where applicable.
